Algebra I · Lesson 4.4

Equations in Disguise

Solve this lesson →All lessons

4.3 ended with a promise, equations that hide the familiar both-sides shape behind fractions and heavier parentheses. This lesson keeps it. Nothing below is new mathematics. Every equation here becomes a 4.2 or 4.3 equation after one cleanup move you already own, and the lesson is learning to see which move each shape calls for.

Problem
Nothing in 4.3 had parentheses wrapped around both sides. Solve 5(2x−3)=3(3x+4)5(2x−3)=3(3x+4) anyway. Distribute on each side the 2.1 way, then collect the 4.3 way, and check in the original before entering the solution.
Show a hint
  • The parentheses are a 2.1 job, not a new rule. Nothing crosses the equals sign until both sides are clean.
  • Distributing on both sides gives 10x−15=9x+1210x−15=9x+12.
Show the full solution
Distribute on each side, 10x−15=9x+1210x−15=9x+12. Subtract 9x9x, x−15=12x−15=12, then add 1515, x=27x=27​. Check, 5(54−3)=2555(54−3)=255 and 3(81+4)=2553(81+4)=255. The parentheses only made the equation look unfamiliar, every move was an old one.
Problem
Solve 7x−2(3x−8)=257x−2(3x−8)=25. The subtracted 22 distributes over both terms of 3x−83x−8, signs included. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • The minus in front of the parentheses belongs to everything inside, both terms.
  • −2(3x−8)−2(3x−8) is −6x+16−6x+16, not −6x−16−6x−16.
Show the full solution
Distribute, 7x−6x+16=257x−6x+16=25, so x+16=25x+16=25 and x=9x=9​. Check, 63−2(27−8)=63−38=2563−2(27−8)=63−38=25. Dropping the sign flip on the 1616 is the single most common slip in this shape.
Key idea
Clean the sides first. Distributing the 2.1 way and combining like terms the 2.4 way rewrite one side as an equal expression, so they change how a side is written, never what it equals, and the other side does not move. Once both sides are clean, 4.2 and 4.3 finish the job. Watch subtracted groups, since a minus in front of parentheses distributes over every term inside, signs and all.

Fractions are the main event. x3+x5=163x​+5x​=16 could be worked the 2.5 way, combining the left side into one fraction, but that drags fractions through every line. 4.2 allows multiplying both sides by any nonzero number, and one well-chosen multiplication removes every fraction at once. Pick a number every denominator divides.

Problem
Solve x3+x5=163x​+5x​=16 by multiplying both sides by 1515, then check in the original before entering the solution.
Show a hint
  • At the solution both sides are the same number, and multiplying both copies by 1515 keeps them equal.
  • Multiplying both sides by 1515 gives 5x+3x=2405x+3x=240.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by 1515, 5x+3x=2405x+3x=240, so 8x=2408x=240 and x=30x=30​. Check, 303+305=10+6=16330​+530​=10+6=16. Multiplying by 1515 cleared both fractions in one step.
Key idea
Clear every denominator in one move. Multiply both sides by a common denominator of every fraction in sight. The move is legal because the multiplier is a known nonzero number, 4.2's rule, and it reaches every term on both sides because multiplication distributes over sums. Each denominator divides the multiplier, so every term comes out whole. The LCD is the smallest number that works, though any common denominator is legal. Then check in the original, since a check against the cleared line cannot catch a mistake made in the clearing.
Problem
Solve x6+x9=106x​+9x​=10. The product 5454 clears both denominators, and so does the LCD 1818, with smaller numbers. Use 1818 and enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • 1818 works because both 66 and 99 divide it.
  • Multiplying both sides by 1818 gives 3x+2x=1803x+2x=180.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by 1818, 3x+2x=1803x+2x=180, so 5x=1805x=180 and x=36x=36​. Check, 6+4=106+4=10. The 5454 route gives 9x+6x=5409x+6x=540 and the same answer, with numbers three times the size.
Problem
Solve x6+5=x46x​+5=4x​. The multiplier 1212 hits every term, the lone 55 included. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • The 55 is a full term of the left side, and the multiplication distributes over the whole side.
  • Clearing with 1212 gives 2x+60=3x2x+60=3x.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by 1212, 2x+60=3x2x+60=3x, so subtracting 2x2x leaves x=60x=60​. Check, 10+5=1510+5=15 and 604=15460​=15. Leaving the 55 unmultiplied is the error this lesson's checks keep catching.
Problem
Solve x+92−x5=62x+9​−5x​=6. The fraction bar groups its numerator, so when you multiply by 1010 the whole x+9x+9 travels together, in parentheses. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • 10⋅x+9210⋅2x+9​ is 5(x+9)5(x+9), never 5x+95x+9.
  • Clearing with 1010 gives 5(x+9)−2x=605(x+9)−2x=60.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by 1010, 5(x+9)−2x=605(x+9)−2x=60, so 3x+45=603x+45=60, 3x=153x=15, and x=5x=5​. Check, 142−1=7−1=6214​−1=7−1=6. The bar is a grouping symbol, doing the same job parentheses do.

When each side of an equation is a single fraction and nothing else, two multiplications clear everything, one for each denominator, and each denominator cancels on its own side. Watch what remains after each cancellation, since the same pattern appears every time this shape does.

Problem
Solve 2x+39=x+7692x+3​=6x+7​. Multiply both sides by a common multiple of the denominators so each one cancels. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • The least common multiple of 99 and 66 is 1818, so multiply both sides by 1818.
  • Clearing the denominators leaves 2(2x+3)=3(x+7)2(2x+3)=3(x+7).
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by 1818, 2(2x+3)=3(x+7)2(2x+3)=3(x+7), so 4x+6=3x+214x+6=3x+21 and x=15x=15​. Check, 339933​ and 226622​ both equal 113311​.
Key idea
Cross-multiplying is two multiplications. Start from ab=cdba​=dc​ with numeric denominators. Multiplying both sides by bb and then by dd leaves ad=bcad=bc, each numerator times the other denominator. People call the shortcut cross-multiplying, and it is 4.2's multiply move run twice, not a new rule. It applies only when each side is one fraction and nothing else. An extra term on either side breaks the pattern, and the full common-denominator multiplier handles those.
Problem
Use the shortcut on 2x+512=x−39122x+5​=9x−3​. The shortcut applies here, since each side is a single fraction and nothing else. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Each numerator multiplies the other denominator, with whole numerators kept in parentheses.
  • The cleared equation is 9(2x+5)=12(x−3)9(2x+5)=12(x−3).
Show the full solution
Cross-multiply, 9(2x+5)=12(x−3)9(2x+5)=12(x−3), so 18x+45=12x−3618x+45=12x−36, 6x=−816x=−81, and x=−272x=−227​​. Check, both sides come out −116−611​. A negative fraction solution is a normal outcome, exactly as in 4.3.

A decimal coefficient is a count of tenths or hundredths, so a decimal equation is a fraction equation. Tenths clear when both sides are multiplied by 1010, hundredths need 100100, and the finest decimal place present picks the power. The move is 4.2's same multiplication, and it hits every term, whole-number constants included.

Problem
Solve 0.8x−3.1=1.70.8x−3.1=1.7 by multiplying both sides by 1010 first, so every count of tenths becomes a whole number. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • Every term is a count of tenths, so multiplying by 1010 makes every coefficient whole.
  • The cleared equation is 8x−31=178x−31=17.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by 1010, 8x−31=178x−31=17, so 8x=488x=48 and x=6x=6​. Check, 4.8−3.1=1.74.8−3.1=1.7.
Problem
Solve 0.06x+4=0.11x+1.50.06x+4=0.11x+1.5. Hundredths call for 100100, and the multiplication turns the whole 44 into 400400. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • Choose the multiplier by the finest decimal place present, and remember it reaches the plain 44 too.
  • Clearing with 100100 gives 6x+400=11x+1506x+400=11x+150.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by 100100, 6x+400=11x+1506x+400=11x+150, so 250=5x250=5x and x=50x=50​. Check, 3+4=73+4=7 and 5.5+1.5=75.5+1.5=7. Multiplying by 1010 instead would leave 1.1x1.1x behind, which is why the finest place picks the power.
Fun fact
In 1202 Leonardo of Pisa, known as Fibonacci, published Liber Abaci, the book that carried Hindu-Arabic numerals and al-Khwarizmi's equation-solving methods into Europe, where merchants and schools took up both.
Problem
A student solves x2−7=x6+42x​−7=6x​+4 by multiplying only the two fractions by 66, writes 3x−7=x+43x−7=x+4, and gets x=112x=211​. That candidate fails the 4.1 check in the original. Multiply every term by 66 and enter the correct solution.
Show a hint
  • A legal multiplication reaches all four terms, the 77 and the 44 included.
  • The correct cleared equation is 3x−42=x+243x−42=x+24.
Show the full solution
Multiply every term by 66, 3x−42=x+243x−42=x+24, so 2x=662x=66 and x=33x=33​. Check, 16.5−7=9.516.5−7=9.5 and 5.5+4=9.55.5+4=9.5. The student's check against the flawed line 3x−7=x+43x−7=x+4 would have passed, which is why a check belongs to the original.

Every multiplier so far was a known nonzero number. In 44x+15=4x+1544​=4 the natural multiplier is x+15x+15, which contains the variable. 4.2's rule still holds wherever x+15x+15 is not zero, ruling out only x=−15x=−15, where the original divides by zero anyway. Clear it, solve, and check in the original, which also shows the denominator was not zero.

Problem
Solve 44x+15=4x+1544​=4. Multiply both sides by x+15x+15, finish with 4.2's moves, and check your value in the original before entering it.
Show a hint
  • After the one multiplication, the equation is a shape 4.2 solved many times.
  • Clearing gives 44=4(x+15)44=4(x+15), so 44=4x+6044=4x+60.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by x+15x+15, 44=4(x+15)44=4(x+15), so 44=4x+6044=4x+60, 4x=−164x=−16, and x=−4x=−4​. Check, −4+15=11−4+15=11 and 4411=41144​=4, so the value works and the denominator was not zero. The check did logical work here, not just hygiene.

Every equation in this lesson stopped looking unfamiliar after one move. Distribute, clear the denominators, or clear the decimals, and each landed in 4.2's or 4.3's hands. 4.5 starts from equations with no algebra written down at all, plain English sentences, and turning those into equations is the next skill.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Solve 4(2x+1)=3(x+8)4(2x+1)=3(x+8).
Show the solution
Distribute on both sides, 8x+4=3x+248x+4=3x+24. Subtract 3x3x, then subtract 44, so 5x=205x=20 and x=4x=4​. Check, both sides equal 3636.
Practice
Solve 9x−4(2x−7)=319x−4(2x−7)=31.
Show the solution
Distribute, 9x−8x+28=319x−8x+28=31, so x+28=31x+28=31 and x=3x=3​. Check, 27−4(−1)=3127−4(−1)=31. Dropping the sign and writing −28−28 is the slip to watch here.
Practice
Solve 4x+35=754x+3​=7.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 55, 4x+3=354x+3=35, so 4x=324x=32 and x=8x=8​. Check, 355=7535​=7.
Practice
Solve x3+x7=203x​+7x​=20.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 2121, 7x+3x=4207x+3x=420, so 10x=42010x=420 and x=42x=42​. Check, 14+6=2014+6=20.
Practice
Solve x2−x6=132x​−6x​=13.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 66, 3x−x=783x−x=78, so 2x=782x=78 and x=39x=39​. Check, 392−132=13239​−213​=13.
Practice
Solve 0.9x−2.5=3.80.9x−2.5=3.8 by multiplying both sides by 1010 first.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 1010, 9x−25=389x−25=38, so 9x=639x=63 and x=7x=7​. Check, 6.3−2.5=3.86.3−2.5=3.8.
Practice
Solve x6=1596x​=915​.
Show the solution
Cross-multiply, 9x=6⋅15=909x=6⋅15=90, so x=10x=10​. Check, both sides equal 5335​.
Practice
Solve x9+4=x69x​+4=6x​. The multiplier reaches the 44 too.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 1818, 2x+72=3x2x+72=3x, so x=72x=72​. Check, 8+4=128+4=12 and 726=12672​=12. Multiplying only the fractions is the error the check would have caught.
Practice
Solve x+87=x−437x+8​=3x−4​.
Show the solution
Cross-multiply, 3(x+8)=7(x−4)3(x+8)=7(x−4), so 3x+24=7x−283x+24=7x−28, then 4x=524x=52 and x=13x=13​. Check, both sides equal 33.
Practice
Solve 0.13x=0.05x+20.13x=0.05x+2.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 100100, 13x=5x+20013x=5x+200, so 8x=2008x=200 and x=25x=25​. Check, 3.25=1.25+23.25=1.25+2.
Practice
Solve x3+8=x2+53x​+8=2x​+5.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 66, 2x+48=3x+302x+48=3x+30. Subtract 2x2x, then subtract 3030, so x=18x=18​. Check, 6+8=146+8=14 and 9+5=149+5=14.
Practice
Solve x8+34=x28x​+43​=2x​. Three fractions, so cross-multiplying does not apply. One multiplier clears all three.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 88, x+6=4xx+6=4x, so 3x=63x=6 and x=2x=2​. Check, 14+34=141​+43​=1.
Practice
Solve x2+x3=−152x​+3x​=−15.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 66, 3x+2x=−903x+2x=−90, so 5x=−905x=−90 and x=−18x=−18​. Check, −9−6=−15−9−6=−15.
Practice
Solve 2x+75=x+12+352x+7​=2x+1​+3. The extra +3+3 means the cross-multiplying shortcut does not apply.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 1010, 2(2x+7)=5(x+1)+302(2x+7)=5(x+1)+30, so 4x+14=5x+354x+14=5x+35 and x=−21x=−21​. Check, −355=−75−35​=−7 and −202+3=−72−20​+3=−7.
Practice
A student solves 0.5x−2=0.25x+4.50.5x−2=0.25x+4.5 by multiplying only the xx terms by 100100, writes 50x−2=25x+4.550x−2=25x+4.5, and gets a candidate that fails the check in the original. Multiply every term by 100100 and enter the correct solution.
Show the solution
Multiply every term by 100100, 50x−200=25x+45050x−200=25x+450, so 25x=65025x=650 and x=26x=26​. Check, 13−2=1113−2=11 and 6.5+4.5=116.5+4.5=11. The student's line skipped the 22 and the 4.54.5, so the two sides were scaled unequally and the candidate fails the original.
Practice
How many solutions does 6x+93=2x+536x+9​=2x+5 have? Enter the count.
Show the solution
The left side is 6x+93=2x+336x+9​=2x+3, so the equation reads 2x+3=2x+52x+3=2x+5. Subtracting 2x2x leaves 3=53=5, which is false, so there are 00​ solutions. The fraction was hiding a 4.3 outcome, not changing it.
Practice
Solve 91x−6=7x−691​=7, and check that your value is not the excluded 66.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by x−6x−6, 91=7(x−6)91=7(x−6), so x−6=13x−6=13 and x=19x=19​. Check, 9113=71391​=7, and 1919 is not the excluded 66, so the denominator was never zero.
Practice
Solve 3x−24−x−36=243x−2​−6x−3​=2. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 1212, 3(3x−2)−2(x−3)=243(3x−2)−2(x−3)=24, so 9x−6−2x+6=249x−6−2x+6=24, then 7x=247x=24 and x=247x=724​​. Check, 2914−114=2814=21429​−141​=1428​=2. Distributing the −2−2 over both terms of x−3x−3 is where this one is usually lost.
